title: How it works
text: FileShare is a thin layer over the tailscale command line tool.

title: How it works
text:
Devices
The device list comes from tailscale status --json. A green dot means the device is online. Taildrop only sends to devices logged in as you.

title: How it works
text:
Sending
Drop files on the window (or click the box to pick them). Each one goes out with:
tailscale file cp <file> <device>:

title: How it works
text:
Receiving
Every 5 seconds the window asks for new files, which runs:
tailscale file get --conflict=rename ~/Downloads/FileShare
Files with the same name are renamed, not overwritten.






Windows and macOS



The official Tailscale app may catch incoming files itself and put them straight into your Downloads folder. So while FileShare is open, any file that newly appears in Downloads is moved into Downloads/FileShare. It can’t tell a Taildrop file from a browser download, so both are moved. Files that were already there when FileShare started are never touched.

title: How it works
text:
Security
FileShare has no network listener of its own. The window talks to a tiny server bound to 127.0.0.1 on a random port, protected by a random per-launch token, so nothing outside your computer can use it.

title: FileShare
text:
FileShare is a small desktop app for moving files between the devices on your Tailscale network. The same window checks for files other devices send you and saves them to ~/Downloads/FileShare.
It is built on Taildrop, Tailscale’s own file sending, so there is nothing to set up on the other side: any device running Tailscale can receive, including phones.

title: FileShare
text:
Why FileShare

One file, no installs. A single Python script using only the standard library.
Works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Opens in its own window when Chrome, Edge or Chromium is installed, otherwise in a browser tab.
Receives automatically. Every 5 seconds it collects anything waiting for you.
Stays on your machine. The window talks to a tiny server on 127.0.0.1, protected by a random per-launch token.

title: Install and run

Get it
Download the repository as a ZIP, or clone it:
git clone https://github.com/GabeAlencar/fileshare.git

title: Install and run
text:
Start it







OS
Start it by




Windows
double-click FileShare.bat (or py fileshare.py)


macOS
double-click FileShare.command (or python3 fileshare.py)


Linux
./fileshare.sh (or python3 fileshare.py)



On macOS and Linux, stop it with Ctrl+C in the terminal. On Windows, end pythonw or use the terminal version.






Linux only, once



Receiving needs permission to talk to Tailscale without sudo:
sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER

title: Install and run
text:
Options







Option
What it does




--downloads DIR
Save received files to DIR instead of ~/Downloads/FileShare


--port N
Serve the window on port N instead of a random one


--no-open
Don’t open a window; just print the URL
